title: MACsec/MKA: Decode using keys unwrapped from MKA messages
description:
Add key derivation, unwrap and storage of SAKs from MKA
Distributed SAK parameter sets and make them available to
the MACsec dissector for use in decryption.

Update MACsec dissector to support multiple configured PSKs.

Add AES-GCM-256 support for MACsec and MKA dissectors.

Correct decode when MACsec SCI is not present.

Add prepend of 'MACsec/' for common protocols in the
COL_PROTOCOL field when they were dissected as part of a
MACsec frame.

A preference can't simply be dropped, it has to be marked obsolete. Otherwise warnings will arise with existing preference files. Preferably its value (in the old preference) would be converted into the new preference, although in these cases that might not be possible.
I can attempt to convert the single PSK into an entry with a default name. I wasn't aware of the 'obsolete' issue.

I cannot find a way to take a preference and convert it to a table entry, as the preference data is not read until after the dissectors are registered(?).  Given it is a single PSK and a relatively recent addition, I think it's simpler to just obsolete it (unless someone can advise).

The TLS dissector has an example of parsing a string preference into a UAT row:
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/epan/dissectors/packet-tls.c#L436

It's a fair amount of work though.
I had worked out how to create the UAT data, but the preference data isn't available at dissector-init time and that's when it seem the previous preference must be obsoleted.  Suggestions?

The TLS dissector actually obsoletes the preference later, on demand when the first time a frame with TLS is encountered (#17051 is related to that). It's an odd duck in that regard.

As a result, if you open up Wireshark and immediately go to the preferences dialog for TLS, you'll see an entry for "RSA keys list (deprecated)".

If you open a capture file that has TLS, and then open the Preferences dialog, the "RSA keys list (deprecated)" entry won't be there any more, because it was marked as obsolete.

I don't think any other dissector does that.

How important is it to obsolete the old preference? I think we
overengineere these things. All that is needed is to save your preferences
again to get rid of the obsolete preference warning.

skrev:

Maybe I am wrong here but are we looking at two different things?

MACsec PSK means a static SAK that could exist without using MKA. While that might not be a smart idea, why would we judge.

The new change is adding the possibility of configuring a CAK into MKA and based on MKA frames dynamically determine the SAKs that MACsec can use.

Shouldn't we leave both options in?

Part of the change converts this from a single PSK to a table of possible PSKs, and the other part adds the ability to additionally use the MKA distributed SAKs to decode.  Both options are available.
So it is not really removing this option but extending it to allow not only a single key. So "only" the configuration has to be changed but the feature is still there.
That's correct.
The AN is not part of the TCI. It takes bits 0 and 1 of octet 3, but as stated in section 9.5: "The TCI field comprises bits 8 through 3 of octet 3 (Figure 9-4) of the SecTAG."
I got a little carried away. :)  I'll fix that up.

changes_data.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,61 @@
+/* packet-mka.h
+ * Routines for MKA packet dissection
+ *
+ * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+ */
+
+#ifndef __PACKET_MKA_H__
+#define __PACKET_MKA_H__
+
+#include <epan/packet.h>
+
+#define AES128_KEY_LEN                  16
+#define AES256_KEY_LEN                  32
+
+#define MACSEC_AN_COUNT                 4
+
+#define MKA_CAK_AES_GCM_128_LEN (AES128_KEY_LEN)
+#define MKA_CAK_AES_GCM_256_LEN (AES256_KEY_LEN)
+#define MKA_MAX_CAK_LEN (MKA_CAK_AES_GCM_256_LEN)
+
+#define MKA_MAX_KEK_LEN (MKA_CAK_AES_GCM_256_LEN)
+#define MKA_MAX_ICK_LEN (MKA_CAK_AES_GCM_256_LEN)
+#define MKA_MAX_SAK_LEN (MKA_CAK_AES_GCM_256_LEN)
+
+typedef struct _mka_ckn_info_key {
+  /* The KEK derived from the CAK */
+  unsigned char kek[MKA_MAX_KEK_LEN];
+  unsigned kek_len;
+
+  /* The ICK derived from the CAK */
+  unsigned char ick[MKA_MAX_ICK_LEN];
+  unsigned ick_len;
+
+  /* the SAKs unwrapped by the KEK for each AN
+   * index is the AN to which the SAK belongs */
+  unsigned char saks[MACSEC_AN_COUNT][MKA_MAX_SAK_LEN];
+
+} mka_ckn_info_key_t;
+
+typedef struct _mka_ckn_info {
+  /* CKN: a byte array of 0 to 32 bytes. */
+  unsigned char *ckn;
+  unsigned ckn_len;
+
+  /* CAK: a byte array of 0 to 32 bytes. */
+  unsigned char *cak;
+  unsigned cak_len;
+
+  /* Identifier for the name of the entry. */
+  unsigned char *name;
+  unsigned name_len;
+
+  /* KEK/ICK/SAK data for this entry */
+  mka_ckn_info_key_t key;
+} mka_ckn_info_t;
+
+/* access to the table data from macsec dissector */
+const mka_ckn_info_t * get_mka_ckn_table(void);
+unsigned get_mka_ckn_table_count(void);
+
+#endif
